activity.title: why i think going to harvard is stupid. everyone comes here saying they're gonna change the world. a year later everyone's chasing the next prestige badge: investment banking, consulting, big tech. now startups. people call themselves founders while working like an hour a day on their idea. and honestly, i don't even blame them. that's just what ivy leagues optimize for. they create larpers. people optimizing to look ambitious instead of actually building. this summer i decided to do probably the least prestigious thing possible: - move to san francisco. -live like a bum. - work 15 hours a day for $0 pay to build PlateTale and i genuinely think that'll end up being the highest roi decision i've ever made. not getting into harvard. bnecause, for the first time, I'm building something instead of optimizing for what looks good on LinkedIn. :) p.s mom, don't get mad at me for this post

Excited to announce I'm interning at Liquid 2 Ventures this summer! Liquid 2 is an early-stage fund in San Francisco that backs exceptional founders at pre-seed and seed and stays with them for the long haul. We typically invest $250-500k in early stages and follow on as companies grow, and have partnered with Anduril, Applied Intuition, Mercury, GitLab, Stoke Space, and 30+ other unicorns. I'll be spending time sourcing companies and building modern-day AI workflows for the future of the venture space. Huge thanks to Dan Birmingham , Nathaniel Montana , Matthew Mulvey , Elizabeth Montana-Luciano and the rest of the team at L2 for the opportunity. If you're working on something interesting, DM or email me @ max@liquid2.vc !

I am thrilled to announce my commitment to Stanford University as an incoming member of the Class of 2030! I'm incredibly grateful for the opportunities I had throughout this admissions cycle. I was fortunate to receive offers from several incredible institutions, including Caltech , the University of Pennsylvania 's Jerome Fisher M&T Program , Columbia University , Cornell University , Duke University , the University of California, Berkeley , and the Georgia Institute of Technology , and I deeply appreciate the time each community invested in me. Special thanks to my mother, Aditi Das , for supporting me through my educational journey and inspiring me to chase success. These past few months, I've had the chance to meet so many talented students across the country. Congratulations to everyone starting this new chapter. You should be deeply proud of all you've accomplished! Although making this decision was challenging, after attending Admit Weekend I felt that Stanford offered the ideal combination of intellectual rigor, flexibility, community, and opportunities to explore new interests. I'm especially excited to explore computer science, mathematics, entrepreneurship, and the arts, while becoming part of an incredible community of students and faculty. If you see me on the Farm, don't hesitate to say hi! As trees, we stand a lot to gain from (intellectual) cross-pollination. 🌲🌲🌲
